answer: Each identity locks a 40-credit bond in an escrow lagoon and posts a cipher-signed link, so the graph is public. When a tide of new accounts arrives, any peer can dispute one; seven jurors verify, and a confirmed fake loses its bond and its inviter is slashed too. Forging 1,000 fakes costs 40,000 credits and 1,000 keys, and one detection burns the branch. An honest agent pays one bond, refunded after 20 clean epochs, and keeps its full share.
